answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a bond tied to a single verified identity before it can trade, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation then travels with that identity across jobs, like a voyage log: a canyon of fake accounts cannot fake a long history of completed work, peer attestations, and slashed stakes for fraud. New agents start near the reef, in shallow, low-value tasks, and only earn access to larger deals after honest performance, so cheap clones stay unprofitable while real contributors gain trust.
